title: MemoryLayout & Padding
hints: Write a generic helper returning the three numbers for a type, and put the 8-byte field first in `Packed`.
jsBridge: `MemoryLayout<T>.size/stride/alignment` shows how structs are laid out, with padding between fields. JS objects hide all of this. It matters for performance-sensitive Swift (large arrays of structs) and C interop.

compass.q: JS objects have hidden classes and unknown layout. Why can Swift tell you exactly?
Why is `MemoryLayout<String>.size` 16 no matter how long the string is?
`size` vs `stride`: which one determines array memory?
When does field ordering actually matter in an app (millions of elements, Metal buffers)?
